text:
sre-jamie: paging  multiple customers in EU and APAC showing intermittent 5xx + certificate mismatches. DNS traces show mixed NS responses: some resolvers returning our primary NS set, others returning an older NS delegation. Appears correlated with a BGP flap in eu-central affecting reachability to our new authoritative nodes.

pagerduty-bot: Incident created: INC-2032. Severity: P1. Notifying on-call.

incident-bot: @sre-jamie acknowledged (02:12 UTC).

netops-li: seeing flaps to one of our authoritative Anycast clusters (eu-auth-2). BGP withdraws reported around 02:08-02:11 from two transit peers. Some public resolvers that hit eu-auth-2 are now receiving stale zone copies from fallback cache (old NS glue).

eng-ravi: application errors look like TLS SNI mismatch when clients hit old edge IPs (we rotated certs last week). That explains cert errors + 5xx. Logs show client IPs from ap-southeast and eu-west mismatching.

sre-jamie: can you paste a couple of dig +trace results from different regions?

netops-li: from us-east1 (good):

```
$ dig +trace api.redwood.xyz @8.8.8.8
; -> .
; ->  ns1.redwood-dns.net 203.0.113.11
; ->  ns2.redwood-dns.net 203.0.113.12
; ANSWER SECTION:
api.redwood.xyz.  300 IN A 203.0.113.101
```

from ap-southeast probe (bad):

```
$ dig +trace api.redwood.xyz @1.1.1.1
; -> .
; ->  ns1.redwood-dns.net 198.51.100.7  ; old-host
; ANSWER SECTION:
api.redwood.xyz.  300 IN A 198.51.100.42
```

netops-li: note different NS glue and IPs (198.51.100.x are decom nodes). TTLs were 600s.

pm-alex: customer impact: multiple paid tiers reported elevated error rates and TLS failures for ~1015m. Need status page update ASAP.

sre-jamie: mitigation options: 1) temporarily re-introduce old NS records globally to canonicalize responses while BGP heals (split-horizon style) 2) force SOA serial bump and lower TTLs for authoritative zone so caches re-query 3) coordinate with transit providers to clear BGP flap quickly 4) request Cloudflare/AWS (where our secondary NS hosted) to purge stale zone copies. Which is least risky?

eng-ravi: reintroducing old NS glue increases surface area and could route more traffic to decom nodes.
I'm leaning to SOA serial bump + TTL drop + edge ACL to blackhole decom IPs.

netops-li: working on transit side now  BGP sessions showing repeated updates to AS64512 peer, support engaged. Pushed a route dampening tweak to reduce churn while we stabilize.

```
# commands being executed (audit)
redwood-dns zone-edit --zone redwood.xyz --soa-serial +1 --ttl 30 --apply
```

netops-li: SOA serial bump and TTL=30 pushed at 02:20 UTC to all authoritative masters. Change propagated to our primary masters; secondaries fetching new zone.

cf-support: Cloudflare support here  we've received SR# CF-2032 and are purging cached zone copies for redwood.xyz in our EU POPs. ETA ~8 minutes.

eng-ravi: deploying network ACLs to drop traffic to known decom IP ranges (198.51.100.0/24) at border routers to avoid cert confusion.

```
# acl rule
acl add drop 198.51.100.0/24 comment "block decom nodes during INC-2032"
```

eng-ravi: ACL applied at 02:28 UTC. Verify if cert errors decrease.

netops-li: after TTL drop + CF purge + ACLs: majority of probes now resolve to correct IPs within one TTL cycle. Some mobile carriers in APAC still returning old answers (likely long-lived resolver caches).

pm-alex: posted preliminary status: "Intermittent DNS resolver inconsistencies caused partial routing to legacy nodes; mitigations in progress. Engineering working with transit and Cloudflare to restore consistent NS answers."

incident-bot: Status page updated: https://status.redwood-inference.example/incidents/INC-2032

eng-ravi: Cloudflare confirms purges completed at 02:36 UTC. Transit partner reports BGP flap suppressed at 02:35 UTC after applying dampening and clearing session.

netops-li: starting a targeted notification to a handful of big ISPs asking for cache clear or guidance (email threads created).

sre-jamie: set monitoring: watch DNS answer diversity metric and TLS mismatch rate. If mismatch rate >5% for 15m escalate to on-call.

incident-bot: Reminder: on-call handoff in 40m.

eng-ravi: exporting request logs and customer error counts for impacted window 01:5502:40 UTC: https://internal-logs.redwood-inference.example/exports/INC-2032-logs

pm-alex: drafting customer note and legal review queued. Will include timeline, cause (BGP flap -> mixed NS answers -> routing to decom nodes), and mitigation steps.

netops-li: post-mitigation checks: external probes in eu/apac show stable NS set; TTL back to 300 at 03:05 UTC after 2 successful probe cycles.

sre-jamie: TTL reset command issued at 03:05 UTC:

```
redwood-dns zone-edit --zone redwood.xyz --ttl 300 --apply
```

incident-bot: Incident INC-2032 moved to Monitoring at 03:06 UTC.

pm-alex: handoff notes for night team: timeline + commands + tickets: CF SR# CF-2032, Transit ticket TR-4521, internal export link. Keep TTL at 300 unless reoccurrence.

eng-ravi: acknowledged handoff (03:19 UTC). Will monitor DNS diversity and TLS mismatch dashboards for the next 6h.

sre-jamie: thanks all. Postmortem requested, include BGP peer metrics and advice to avoid simultaneous zone reconfigs during transit maintenance windows. Closing thread and moving to formal incident doc.

pagerduty-bot: Incident INC-2032 status changed to Monitoring at 03:06 UTC."
